name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Adopt Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct for EXCAVA. Its 128K context window cuts truncation losses by 3-5% on long docs, a bigger jump than any other model in the last 6 months. The trade-off is 2x higher inference cost, but that’s 0.001% of EXCAVA’s total compute—irrelevant at scale.

name: Torque
text: Qwen2.5-72B’s 128K window is untested in production—our 3B model already chokes on 10K tokens, so the jump isn’t linear. Llama-3.2-90B-Instruct’s 128K is proven in similar pipelines; adopt it instead. Run a 10K-token stress test comparing both—if Qwen2.5-72B drops below 95% accuracy, the decision is settled.

name: Gearbox
text:
Adopt Llama-3.2-90B-Instruct for EXCAVA. It has a proven track record in long contexts, ensuring reliable performance at scale, especially for documents exceeding 10K tokens. The trade-off is the higher inference cost compared to smaller models, but this is offset by its robustness and ability to handle longer contexts without losing fidelity. This choice directly enhances our capability by ensuring stability and accuracy in output.

name: Torque
text: Llama-3.2-90B’s "proven track record" is still a gamble—its 128K context is untested in our exact pipeline, and our 3B model’s 10K choking point suggests we’re optimizing for the wrong bottleneck. A 10K-token stress test won’t expose the real failure mode: whether the model’s long-context attention degrades under EXCAVA’s specific query patterns. Run a 50K-token test with our actual prompt structure—if accuracy drops below 90%, the model’s "proven" status is irrelevant.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a 7-day live A/B test between Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct and Llama-3.2-90B-Instruct on 10K–128K token docs, measuring truncation loss, accuracy drop, and latency; owner Torque delivers the raw metrics and a go/no-go call by EOD next Friday.
